We need retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have hints: step1 forward: carboxylic acid to amide (coupling). So retrosynthesis: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step2 forward: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the double bond). So retrosynthesis: break C=C double bond and carboxylic acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid? Actually forward: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid (with decarboxylation). So reverse: from unsaturated acid we can get aldehyde + malonic acid. In our target, we have /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid part is /C=C/C(=O)N... The unsaturated acid is attached to aromatic ring via double bond. So we can retrosynthetically disconnect the C=C double bond to give aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). But also the amide is attached to the unsaturated acid carbonyl. So step1 will later convert that acid to amide with aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step2: break the double bond and the carboxylic acid to give aldehyde and malonic acid.

Step3 forward: sulfonamide formation: amine + sulfonyl chloride -> sulfonamide. So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride (ArSO2Cl) and amine (the aniline ring). In target, we have NS(=O)(=O) attached to phenyl ring (c1ccc...). So we can disconnect to give sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl (c1ccc(SO2Cl)cc1) and the amine (the other phenyl with NH2). Actually sulfonamide is between the first phenyl (with methyl) and the second phenyl (with unsaturated amide). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (with methyl) and the sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl. So retrosynthesis: break N-S bond to give sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2) and aniline (c1ccc(NH2)cc1 with methyl). Wait the first phenyl has methyl substituent (C). So we need aniline with methyl (p-toluidine). So step3: sulfonyl chloride + p-toluidine -> sulfonamide.

Thus overall route:

Target (M0) -> step1 (retro amide formation): break amide to give unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH attached to second phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to phenyl (c3ccccc3N). So product after step1: unsaturated acid (C=C-COOH attached to second phenyl) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). Step2: retro Doebner: unsaturated acid -> aromatic aldehyde (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) + malonic acid. Step3: retro sulfonamide: sulfonyl chloride attached to second phenyl (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2) + p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1). Wait we also need to incorporate the aldehyde? Actually after step2 we have aldehyde attached to phenyl (c2ccc(CHO)cc2). This aldehyde will be used to make unsaturated acid via Doebner with malonic acid. The sulfonyl chloride is attached to same phenyl? In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl (the one bearing the unsaturated amide). So after step2 we have aldehyde phenyl (c2ccc(CHO)cc2). To get sulfonyl chloride attached to that phenyl, we need to have sulfonyl chloride on that phenyl before Doebner? Actually forward: sulfonamide formation is separate: the sulfonyl chloride reacts with amine to give sulfonamide linking the two phenyl rings. In target, the sulfonyl group is attached to the second phenyl (the one with unsaturated amide). The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the first phenyl (p-tolyl). So the sulfonyl chloride precursor is the second phenyl with SO2Cl substituent (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2). This sulfonyl chloride will later be coupled with p-toluidine to give sulfonamide. The unsaturated acid is attached to that phenyl via the double bond at para position relative to sulfonyl? In SMILES: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2 attached to S(=O)(=O) to the first phenyl. So the sulfonyl chloride is on the second phenyl at para position relative to the side chain? Actually the SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. So the sulfonyl group attached to the second phenyl (c2ccc...). The side chain is para to the sulfonyl? Not needed.

Thus retrosynthesis steps:

1. Break amide: product A: unsaturated acid attached to second phenyl (call fragment F1): c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 (with sulfonyl attached later) Actually after breaking amide we have carboxylic acid (instead of amide). So fragment: c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)O)cc2 attached to sulfonyl? The sulfonyl is still attached to that phenyl, yes. So we have sulfonyl phenyl with unsaturated acid.

And fragment B: aniline (c3ccccc3N) (the amine that will be coupled later).

2. Retro Doebner on fragment A: break unsaturated acid to give aldehyde phenyl (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) with sulfonyl attached, and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH).

3. Retro sulfonamide: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride attached to aldehyde phenyl (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2) and p-toluidine (Cc1ccc(NH2)cc1).

Thus final precursors: p-toluidine, sulfonyl chloride phenyl aldehyde, malonic acid, aniline? Wait we already have aniline as product of step1, but after step3 we have p-toluidine and sulfonyl chloride phenyl aldehyde. The aniline from step1 is separate; it will be coupled later with the acid (step1 forward). So final set of starting materials: p-toluidine (C methyl phenyl amine), sulfonyl chloride phenyl aldehyde (c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2 with aldehyde? Actually the aldehyde is on same phenyl as sulfonyl? In target, the aldehyde is not present; after Doebner, the aldehyde becomes unsaturated acid. So the sulfonyl chloride phenyl should have aldehyde substituent at para position relative to sulfonyl? In SMILES, the side chain is attached at para to sulfonyl? The SMILES: NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2. The sulfonyl attached to phenyl at position 1, side chain at position 4. So the aldehyde precursor would be c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2 with aldehyde at para? Actually the aldehyde is the precursor to side chain, so the phenyl would have aldehyde at para to sulfonyl: c2ccc(SO2Cl)cc2 with CHO at para. So the sulfonyl chloride phenyl aldehyde: 4-formyl-4'-chlorosulfonyl? Wait sulfonyl chloride is at position 1, aldehyde at position 4. So SMILES: O=ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(cc1)C=O? Actually aldehyde attached to phenyl: c1ccc(S(=O)(=O)Cl)cc1C=O? Need correct SMILES: "O=ClS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(cc1)C=O". That is para? Might be okay.

Also need malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So total 4 starting materials, but route has 3 reactions.

Now we need to find template IDs for each retrosynthetic step. Use search_template_catalog_by_criteria for each transformation.

Step1: amide formation forward: carboxylic acid + amine -> amide. Retro: break amide to acid + amine. So functional_groups_broken: amide? Actually forward forms amide, breaks carboxylic acid (C-O) and N-H? The hint says carbon-nitrogen bond formed while carbon-oxygen broken as result of breaking aliphatic carboxylic acid. So we search for templates where functional_groups_broken includes "aliphatic carboxylic acid" and functional_groups_formed includes "amide". Use that.
